purpose: The Topics computation-cost baseline: the figures quoted in 2026-09-20-topics-computation-cost-baseline.md, each extracted from the run that produced it.

machine.caveat: The two matrix arms ran on a shared machine under unrelated Deno, Python and Xcode load, and under markedly asymmetric contention: the on arm's one-minute load had a median of 24.18 over 22 samples, the off arm's 10.24 over 26. The more contended arm is the faster one, so contention does not account for the elapsed-time difference between them; two single samples do not make a latency baseline either way. The alternating repeat subset, which the timing claims rest on, ran later at a median one-minute load of 6.54 over 16 samples, and alternates the arms so that drift falls on both.

machine.note: Shared machine under unrelated load throughout; see loadSeries.
machine.browser: Google Chrome 153, the installed browser Astral was pointed at.
machine.sandbox: The session was unsandboxed. Established by capability rather than by configuration: writes outside the workspace, Apple Events, the GUI launchd domain and direct network all succeeded.

boardWorkloadNotMeasured.reason: A board loaded before any topic is opened reads its stored card values, and in a browser with client execution loading it ran none of the reached lifts, so there is no work of theirs to measure headlessly. Returning to the board after opening a topic ran that topic's last activity once; that state is not one of the probe's workloads.

startupAndLatencyDerivation.note: The observations the plan's startup and latency limits are derived from, and the arithmetic. The limits themselves are recorded in the measurement-and-acceptance section of docs/plans/topics-computation-cost.md; this block is the derivation, not a second statement of the policy. Taken under client execution on a shared machine under unrelated load; sources.browser and loadByArm record the conditions. Not gated in continuous integration.
